assessment.nobel_worthiness: A foundational economic framework for valuing exhaustible natural capital, biodiversity, and intergenerational welfare, with major consequences for environmental policy.
assessment.attribution: Dasgupta and Heal are central architects of the listed contribution; the two-person formulation gives unusually clear credit.
assessment.maturity: The work has had decades to shape environmental and resource economics and has gained broad policy relevance.
uncertainties: The breadth of the modern biodiversity and inclusive-wealth literature makes the precise boundary of a prize citation consequential.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The misallocation framework made a powerful, quantitatively operational connection between distorted factor allocation and large productivity and income gaps.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh and Klenow supplied the especially influential empirical-quantitative formulation, while Restuccia is a leading contributor to the broader mechanism.
assessment.maturity: The approach is well established across growth and development research and has generated a substantial subsequent literature.
uncertainties: The appropriate division between the core Hsieh-Klenow contribution and the broader misallocation literature is not fully settled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Modern New Keynesian analysis supplied a coherent framework for studying nominal rigidities, monetary policy, and stabilization in dynamic general equilibrium.
assessment.attribution: Woodford, Calvo, and Gali are highly defensible representatives of the core theoretical synthesis, though the long credited list reflects genuinely distributed contributions.
assessment.maturity: The framework has been central to monetary economics, policy analysis, and macroeconomic research for many years.
uncertainties: Attribution is difficult because several listed researchers made indispensable complementary contributions.
The extent to which one unified prize contribution can encompass the full New Keynesian framework is debatable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This body of political-economy research transformed the analysis of how political institutions, accountability, and state capacity shape economic policy and development.
assessment.attribution: Persson and Tabellini provided core formal institutional analysis, and Besley made central contributions linking political incentives and state capacity.
assessment.maturity: The work is longstanding, cumulative, and deeply integrated into political economy and public-finance research.
uncertainties: The contribution spans several related institutional mechanisms rather than a single sharply bounded discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection fundamentally altered the analysis of trade, productivity, reallocation, and the gains from globalization.
assessment.attribution: Melitz is the indispensable originator of the canonical model; Helpman and Redding are major contributors to its extension and empirical-theoretical development.
assessment.maturity: The framework has become a standard part of modern international trade and has accumulated extensive empirical and policy applications.
uncertainties: A citation centered on the canonical model could raise questions about how broadly to share credit for the larger research program.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Partial identification changed empirical economics by making transparent what data can establish under credible, limited assumptions rather than imposing point identification.
assessment.attribution: Manski is the foundational figure; Tamer and Molinari made important advances in moment inequalities and practical inference.
assessment.maturity: The ideas are mature and influential across econometrics and applied work where conventional identification is untenable.
uncertainties: The broad partial-identification tradition contains additional contributors whose exclusion may be contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Models of collateral constraints and financial amplification gave macroeconomics essential tools for understanding credit cycles and crisis propagation.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore are central to collateral-based amplification, while Gertler made major contributions to the financial-accelerator framework.
assessment.maturity: The mechanisms were established well before the global financial crisis and became even more central afterward.
uncertainties: The financial-accelerator literature has multiple closely connected formulations and the appropriate laureate set is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The integration of insurance-market theory with credible measurement substantially improved understanding of adverse selection, pricing, and welfare.
assessment.attribution: Finkelstein and Einav are leading empirical-theoretical contributors, while Salanie is a central architect of the relevant insurance-economics framework.
assessment.maturity: The contribution has generated a durable literature and has clear implications for health, insurance, and public policy.
uncertainties: The cited contribution combines theory and several empirical settings, which can make a single attribution boundary difficult.
